entry.title: SpaceX to Build Texas Foundry for Turbine Blades to Support AI Power Needs
entry.content:
Techmeme | theinformation.com

SpaceX is establishing a manufacturing facility in Bastrop, Texas, to produce blades for large gas turbines. This move aims to vertically integrate the company's power supply chain and address the energy shortages currently affecting the expansion of AI data centers.

Job listings for automation engineers specializing in blades and vanes suggest the facility will focus on advanced casting techniques. These components are intended to serve both data center power generation and the production of Starship's Raptor engine turbopumps.

entry.title: Organizational Culture Over AI Tools for Maximizing Engineering Productivity
entry.content:
Hacker News Best | newsletter.eng-leadership.com | hacker news

High-performing engineering teams rely more on healthy organizational environments than on the implementation of AI tools to drive productivity. Because AI acts as an amplifier, it accelerates high performance in healthy organizations but can exacerbate bad communication or poor architecture in dysfunctional ones.

Based on Conway's Law, a company's communication structure dictates its technical output. Effective AI adoption requires a leadership-driven cultural foundation rather than top-down mandates, prioritizing psychological safety and clear outcomes over simple tool deployment.

entry.title: DHS Uses Customs Law to Obtain Data on Journalists and Non-Profits
entry.content:
Hacker News Best | theguardian.com | hacker news

The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) is using an obscure customs law, 19 USC 1509, to issue administrative summonses for private information from journalists, non-profits, and labor unions. These summonses allow the agency to obtain data—including telephone records and social media account information—without judicial oversight or the need to establish probable cause.

Legal experts argue the maneuver allows the government to bypass Fourth Amendment protections by utilizing customs-enforcement powers for domestic investigations. The strategy has been used to target political activists, journalists, and various organizations, including efforts to uncover social media identities and the financial records of activist groups.

entry.title: Sony Music Publishing and Warner Chappell Music Sue Anthropic
entry.content:
Techmeme | musicbusinessworldwide.com | source

Sony Music Publishing and Warner Chappell Music have sued Anthropic and its co-founders for allegedly using tens of thousands of copyrighted musical compositions to train Claude AI models. The lawsuit, filed in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California, alleges the company utilized illegal torrenting and scraping from sources like Library Genesis to harvest intellectual property.

The publishers are seeking statutory damages, the destruction of infringing copies, and a formal account of Claude’s training data. The filing follows a series of similar copyright infringement lawsuits filed against Anthropic by other major industry players, including Universal Music Publishing Group and BMG.
